direction: Improve the guided-insertion seed + 2-opt repair hook so that the 500 ms budget is spent where it pays: (1) build a k-NN candidate graph (k = min(20, n-1)) once and reuse it for both insertion scoring and move generation; (2) make the insertion phase regret-aware instead of pure best-insertion — score_insertion_move should return a lexicographic score (best insertion cost, then second-best minus best, i.e. regret) so high-regret cities are placed first, which fixes the chevron/stranded-city failures that dominate the size=50 and size=100 regimes; (3) follow with neighbor-restricted first-improvement 2-opt using don't-look bits plus an Or-opt (segment of 1-3 nodes) pass, restarting 2-opt only on nodes touched by an accepted move; (4) guard the total against the deadline with a decreasing-iteration check scaled by n (n<=60 -> full candidate sweep; n>=150 -> cap candidate width to ~8 and skip Or-opt when the remaining time fraction is low), so larger instances degrade gracefully rather than exhausting the budget mid-move.

operations.mechanism: Round-2 solver cut mean objective from 87950.84 to 85145.85 (delta -2804.99) using the same template, so the template family is still on the improving side of the Pareto curve; the archive shows solver_count=2 with a 0.55% gap over SBS and only 6/36 instances won by the older variant, meaning the search-space around this template is not yet exhausted. All three weakest regimes are size-bucketed (50/100/200) with negative rel gaps and zero exhausted/failed instances, i.e. quality-limited, not budget-limited — so the lever is move-phase efficiency (candidate lists, don't-look bits, regret ordering) rather than raising raw iteration counts. KB entries confirm the official construct is a k-NN list plus nearest-neighbor argmin, and that neighbor-restricted 2-opt on a geometric k-nearest graph is the canonical repair, so the proposed hook stays inside the allowed template contract while changing only the scoring/ordering policy.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: Regret-based (forced-early) insertion seeded from a k-NN candidate graph, followed by neighbor-restricted 2-opt with don't-look bits and an Or-opt segment pass, lowers mean tour length on tsp dev_24 relative to pure best-insertion + geometric 2-opt at the same ~500 ms budget, with the largest gain in the size=50 and size=100 regimes (current vbs_rel_gap of -16.06% and -14.31%), because regret ordering prevents expensive late insertions on nearly-closed tours while don't-look bits let the 2-opt phase exhaust improving moves on small n instead of spending the budget re-scanning all pairs.
